kjv: what the LORD did because of Baal-peor
note: Hebrew be-ba'al pe'or can mean "at (the place) Baal-peor" or "in the matter of (the god) Baal of Peor"; the KJV takes the causal sense.

mine: that has a god so near to it
note: Hebrew 'elohim qerovim, with a plural adjective, refers to any nation's god(s) in comparison with Yahweh; the KJV's capitalised "God" blurs the comparison.

kjv: if thou turn to the LORD thy God
mine: you will return to Yahweh your God
note: The Hebrew perfects with waw (ve-shavta, ve-shama'ta; cf. u-viqqashtem in v.29) read most naturally as a prediction that Israel will return in the latter days; the KJV turns vv.29-30 into conditions ("if thou shalt seek ... if thou turn"). Context: you will return (prediction) (high confidence). The waw-perfects ve-shavta, ve-shama'ta continue the future of 4:29 ('you will seek ... you will find'), and 30:1-3 predicts the same return in exile. LXX reads a future. ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV and NJPS all render a prediction. Other possible meanings: (1) a condition, 'if you turn to Yahweh your God and obey his voice' — KJV, Geneva; a waw-perfect after a temporal clause can carry conditional force; (2) an exhortation, 'then return to Yahweh your God' — some commentators.
Hebrew ha-nissah 'elohim in this rhetorical comparison means "has any god attempted"; KJV "God" suggests the true God.
Hebrew massot means tests or trials (the plagues as ordeals), not enticements to sin as "temptations" now implies.

kjv: brought thee out in his (Yahweh's) sight
note: Hebrew be-fanav, "with his presence/face", means Yahweh brought them out personally, not merely while watching.

mine: prolong your days in the land
note: Hebrew ha-'adamah here is the specific land Yahweh is giving Israel, not the earth at large.
Hebrew 'ashdot means slopes or mountain-sides, not springs (cf. 3:17, where the KJV transliterates it).
